title: A universal emulator for planar Ising lattices
authors: Riccardo Ben Alì Zinati, Alessandro Codello
abstract: We introduce the notion of an Ising emulator for two-dimensional Ising models: flat, unit-edge-length lattices can be represented as site- or bond-diluted supercells of a single host lattice, for which the Feynman--Vdovichenko/Kac--Ward solution is fixed once and for all. We construct explicit square and triangular emulators and show that a single transition matrix, supplemented by lattice-specific binary masks, gives all the thermodynamic quantities of interest for both ferro- and antiferromagnetic couplings. We apply the framework to all eleven Archimedean lattices, to all twenty $2$-uniform lattices -- whose thermodynamics is obtained here for the first time -- and to several pentagonal lattices, and show that the same construction extends directly to fractal and disordered Ising models, with no modification to the underlying machinery.
summary: This paper introduces a universal emulator framework to calculate the thermodynamics of Ising models on any planar lattice. By embedding complex target lattices into a fixed, simple host lattice structure, the authors derive all necessary thermodynamic quantities using a single mathematical machinery based on the Feynman–Vdovichenko/Kac–Ward solution. This greatly expands the scope of solvable models in 2D statistical mechanics.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a universal computational framework (an 'emulator') for calculating the thermodynamic properties of two-dimensional Ising models on arbitrary planar lattices.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrate that this single construction, based on embedding any target lattice into a host lattice, can calculate observables for all Archimedean and many other complex planar geometries.
method: The method utilizes the Feynman–Vdovichenko/Kac–Ward (FV/KW) solution, representing the partition function via a determinant involving a transition matrix derived from the lattice's connectivity masks.
model_or_system: The system is the 2D Ising model ($\pm J$) defined on various planar lattices ($\Lambda$). These target lattices are computationally realized by embedding them as site- or bond-diluted supercells within a fixed host lattice (e.g., square or triangular).
key_observables: Free energy, internal energy, specific heat capacity, critical temperatures ($T_c$), and entropy for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic couplings.
important_parameters: The coupling constants ($\xi = \pm 1$), temperature ($T$), and the lattice momenta $(k_1, k_2)$ used in the momentum integral are crucial parameters.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the thermodynamics depends only on the topology of the target lattice $[\Lambda]$, allowing a single host-based machinery to calculate results for diverse geometries.
figures_summary: The notes indicate extensive tables summarizing calculated thermodynamic properties (Free energy, Entropy, Energy per spin, Specific heat) across numerous simulated lattices and varying temperature regimes.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the general emulator concept using a fixed host matrix ($\mathbf{W}_{\mathcal{H}}$), details its application to specific hosts (square/triangular), and then systematically applies this framework to calculate observables for large sets of known and novel planar lattices, culminating in comparative tables.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the concept of using a fixed 'hardware' structure (the host matrix) parameterized by 'software' masks (binary occupation patterns) is analogous to modern computational modeling techniques used in quantum simulation or circuit design.
